It's funny, isn't it? Lager gets a bad name from ale connoisseurs, but it is significantly harder to brew.

I'm one of those darker is better types, but I do like a good ruby here and there.

I love beers of all colors. Fizzy and yellow (Holla, Green Flash) and dark and strong (Yeti!) and everything in between. Lagers, I think, get a bad rap largely because the American Lager (US version of Budweiser) isn't a really interesting or complicated taste profile. I'm not a fan of its flavor.

I do, however, have utmost respect for the difficulty of brewing that much beer that has so little variation in flavor. It really isn't easy to accomplish such consistency on such a large scale.
